papers.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
papers.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

papers.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics
papers.abstract: Optical neural networks (ONNs) are attracting significant attention as alternative platforms for machine learning (ML). In an ONN, an optical module often takes over part of the computation inside a digital ML pipeline. How much of the task does the optical module itself perform, and how much does it contribute to any claimed system-level advantages, such as throughput or energy? This paper offers a simple, function-oriented evaluation methodology. Whatever its internal physics, the optical module appears to the surrounding digital pipeline as a mapping between real-valued tensors. We therefore evaluate it in three steps: (i) define its boundary in the pipeline, as real-valued tensors in and out; (ii) replace it with standard digital modules to identify those that match the optical system's performance on the same task and metric; and (iii) state system-level claims, such as speed or energy, per inference against the performance-matched digital module. We summarize steps (i) and (ii) in an Expressivity Card and demonstrate its use on published ONN systems. This helps isolate the optical module's contribution and provides a concrete digital reference for assessing its claimed system-level advantages, without the need to understand the physics. While we focus on optical systems as the most prominent example, the same approach applies to any physical analog computing platform used in ML, wherever a physical module takes over part of a digital pipeline.

papers.title: Observation of room-temperature intrinsic antiferroelectricity in van der Waals NbOCl2
papers.abstract: In recent years, two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectricity has been extensively investigated across a wide range of 2D materials, while intrinsic 2D antiferroelectricity remains exceptionally rare, limiting its implementation in next-generation photonic and electronic devices. Here, we report the observation of room-temperature-stable antiferroelectricity in the layered transition metal oxyhalide NbOCl2, and demonstrate a reversible, stimuli-driven antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric (AFE-to-FE) phase transition in this material. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) mapping reveals a well-defined stripe-like spatial distribution of SHG intensity across as-grown NbOCl2 flakes spanning thickness from few-layer to bulk-like configurations. This distinctive SHG signature originates from the existence of antiferroelectric phase and the coexistence of antiferroelectric and ferroelectric phases within individual crystals, as evidenced by a combined incident-angle-dependent SHG measurement and Raman spectroscopy. By integrating NbOCl2 with one-dimensional silver nanowires, we achieve spatially selective, strain-mediated AFE-to-FE phase transition. Moreover, an ultralow electric field (~20 kV/cm) induces a reversible SHG response, consistent with switching from the centrosymmetric antiferroelectric state (SHG-silent) to the non-centrosymmetric ferroelectric state (SHG-active). This study not only expands the family of room-temperature 2D antiferroelectrics but also establishes a versatile platform for dynamic manipulation of nonlinear light, paving the way toward electric-field-programmable nonlinear photonics and optical information processing.

papers.title: Mid-Infrared Integrated Acousto-Optic Phase Modulation on GaAs/AlGaAs
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a mid-infrared (7.5-10 um) integrated acousto-optic phase modulator operating at 460MHz based on a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure. The combination of broad mid-infrared transparency and piezoelectric properties of GaAs based structures allows monolithic integration of all the device functions (electro-acoustic transduction and acousto-optic interaction) on a single material platform. Addressing the challenge presented by comparable mid-infrared and acoustic wavelengths, simultaneous propagation and confinement of surface acoustic waves and guided light is achieved using a deep-etched sub-wavelength grating. We develop a comprehensive and quantitative simulation framework to design the modulator devices, characterize their acoustic properties in a heterodyne vibrometer and perform a full, quantitative analysis of the device performance by inserting them in an integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Remarkable agreement with simulations validates the proposed design flow, and opens the way to improved integrated acousto-optic devices operating in the longer end of the mid-infrared.

papers.title: Thermoelectric properties of metal-semiconductor percolation composites
papers.abstract: We analyze the thermoelectric response of composite materials comprising homogeneous semiconductor hosts with randomly distributed metallic inclusions. We demonstrate that the properties of such materials are strongly affected by the percolation transition (with background conductivity). We show that in the vicinity of the percolation threshold, the power factor and the thermoelectric figure of merit strongly depend on both the concentration and arrangement of inclusions. Finally, we identify promising regimes for enhancing the power factor in realistic composites.

papers.title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
papers.abstract: The hot carrier solar cell exhibits a photovoltaic conversion efficiency limit of 85.4%. Among the idealizations necessary to achieve this efficiency, it has traditionally been considered essential that the electrons absorbing sunlight do not end up transferring the captured energy to the crystal lattice. In this work, we argue that such a requirement is not necessary if the absorber is thermally insulated. In our analysis, we also consider the possibility of ohmic losses in the absorber due to finite electrical conductivity. We also demonstrate that such losses, delivered as heat, can be partially recycled into electrical work with an efficiency that is given by the Carnot factor. The high efficiencies reported here are thermodynamic limits obtained with ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance, not projections of practical device efficiency. Our work includes a sensitivity analysis for finite contact-mediated heat leakage, and the results are presented as design targets.

papers.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
papers.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{max} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{br}I_{max}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

papers.title: Generation of neutron Bessel beams
papers.abstract: Matter waves can exhibit structured wavefields analogous to those of light, offering new means of controlling the spatial and angular-momentum degrees of freedom of massive particles. Bessel beams are a fundamental class of structured waves that exhibit non-diffracting propagation, self-healing, and well-defined orbital angular momentum (OAM). Here, we experimentally realize neutron Bessel beams by imprinting a nanoscale conical phase gradient onto a neutron wavefront. By incorporating azimuthal phase gradients, we generate zeroth-, third-, and sixth-order Bessel beams, demonstrating direct control of both the OAM and radial structure of a massive particle. We also propose a neutron Bessel-grating interferometer, complementary to established optical and electron interferometric methods, in which varying the radial grating period by approximately 100 nm yields a controlled Gouy phase shift of $\pi$. These results establish neutron Bessel beams as a new platform for diffractive neutron focusing and provide an experimental foundation for theoretical studies of Bessel beams in neutron scattering, decay, and OAM characterization.

papers.title: Closer look at some sum uncertainty relations and related relations: Their weak points
papers.abstract: We analyze the weak and critical points of some state--dependent uncertainty relations that follow from the inequalities for the norms of vectors in the Hilbert space of states of a quantum system. Uncertainty relations for sums of standard deviations, for sums of variances, and other relations between standard deviations or variances are studied. The obtained results are compared with the conclusions obtained in similar cases using the standard Heisenberg--Robertson uncertainty relation. We also show that, in critical cases, the right--hand sides of sum and stronger sum uncertainty relations provide similar information regarding lower bounds on the left--hand sides of these relations as the Heisenberg--Robertson uncertainty relations do. New reverse uncertainty relations for a sum of variances are derived.

papers.title: FPGA-based LQG controller and hardware-in-the-loop simulator implementation for nanomechanical systems
papers.abstract: We present an open-source framework for real-time Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation on the affordable Red Pitaya STEMlab FPGA platform. The controller implements a discrete-time Kalman filter and Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) for systems with up to three coupled oscillatory degrees of freedom, targeting applications in levitated optomechanics, MEMS/NEMS, and related experimental platforms. Complementing the controller, the HIL simulator provides a~configurable second-order stochastic plant with nonlinear input and output mappings, enabling realistic closed-loop testing under real-time and fixed-point constraints. A MATLAB-based workflow automates model configuration, controller synthesis, numerical scaling, and FPGA deployment without requiring specialized hardware expertise. As an end-to-end demonstration, we present the stabilization of a levitated nanoparticle in a two-dimensional double-well potential, illustrating the complete workflow from model definition and simulation to real-time feedback control. The codebase: https://github.com/TU-Wien-ACIN-CDS/FPGA-based-LQG-and-HIL-simulator-for-nanomechanical-systems
